subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following stating the rules used.
solution:
\(\sim [(p \vee q) \wedge (q \vee \sim r)] \equiv \sim (p \vee q) \vee \sim (q \vee \sim r)\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee (\sim q \wedge r)\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv (\sim q \wedge \sim p) \vee (\sim q \wedge r)\) [Commutative law]
\(\equiv \sim q \wedge (\sim p \vee r)\) [Distributive law]

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following stating the rules used.
solution:
\(\sim [(p \to q) \vee r] \equiv \sim (p \to q) \wedge \sim r\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv (p \wedge \sim q) \wedge \sim r\) [\(\sim (p \to q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q\)]

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following stating the rules used.
solution:
\(\sim [p \wedge (q \vee r)] \equiv \sim p \vee \sim (q \vee r)\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv \sim p \vee (\sim q \wedge \sim r)\) [DeMorgan's law]

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following stating the rules used.
solution:
\(\sim [(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \equiv \sim (\sim p \wedge q) \wedge \sim (p \wedge \sim q)\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv (p \vee \sim q) \wedge (\sim p \vee q)\) [DeMorgan's law]

subtopic: Quantifiers, Duality and Negation of Statements
context: Write the negations of the following stating the rules used.
solution:
\(\sim [(p \wedge q) \to (\sim p \vee r)] \equiv (p \wedge q) \wedge \sim (\sim p \vee r)\) [\(\sim (p \to q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q\)]
\(\equiv (p \wedge q) \wedge [p \wedge \sim r]\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv q \wedge p \wedge p \wedge \sim r\) [Associative law]
\(\equiv q \wedge p \wedge \sim r\) [Idempotent law]

subtopic: Converse, Inverse and Contrapositive
context: Rewrite the following statements without using if ...... then.
stem: If prices increase then the wages rise.
solution:
Let \(p\) : Prices increase, \(q\) : The wages rise.
The given statement is \(p \to q\) but \(p \to q \equiv \sim p \vee q\).
The given statement can be written as 'Prices do not increase or the wages rise'.

subtopic: Converse, Inverse and Contrapositive
context: Rewrite the following statements without using if ...... then.
stem: If it is cold, then we wear woolen clothes.
solution:
Let \(p\) : It is cold, \(q\) : We wear woollen clothes.
The given statement is \(p \to q\) but \(p \to q \equiv \sim p \vee q\).
The given statement can be written as 'It is not cold or we wear woollen clothes'.

subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
context: Without using truth table prove that :
solution:
We know that \(p \leftrightarrow q \equiv (p \to q) \wedge (q \to p)\)
\(\equiv (\sim p \vee q) \wedge (\sim q \vee p)\) [Conditional law]
\(\equiv \sim (p \wedge \sim q) \wedge \sim (q \wedge \sim p)\) [DeMorgan's law]

subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
context: Without using truth table prove that :
solution:
\(\sim (p \vee q) \vee (\sim p \wedge q) \equiv (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee (\sim p \wedge q)\) [DeMorgan's law]
\(\equiv \sim p \wedge (\sim q \vee q)\) [Distributive law]
\(\equiv \sim p \wedge t\) [Complement law]
\(\equiv \sim p\) [Identity law]

subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
context: Without using truth table prove that :
solution:
\((p \vee q) \wedge \sim p \equiv \sim p \wedge (p \vee q)\) [Commutative law]
\(\equiv (\sim p \wedge p) \vee (\sim p \wedge q)\) [Distributive law]
\(\equiv c \vee (\sim p \wedge q)\) [Complement law]
\(\equiv \sim p \wedge q\) [Identity law]
